title: Say, tell, explain and suggest
what: the wrong pattern after reporting verbs ('He said me that', 'She told that she was late', 'Can you explain me', 'He suggested me to wait')
summary: These errors persist due to L1 interference and overgeneralization of 'tell' patterns. They subtly disrupt natural English flow, making communication less precise and marking speech as non-native.
listenFor: Pay close attention to the grammatical structures immediately following 'say,' 'tell,' 'explain,' and 'suggest' in your own speech.

contrasts.wrong: He said me that the meeting was postponed until next week.
contrasts.right: He said that the meeting was postponed until next week.
contrasts.note: 'Say' does not take a direct object pronoun before a 'that' clause.

contrasts.wrong: She told that she would be late for the presentation.
contrasts.right: She told us that she would be late for the presentation.
contrasts.note: 'Tell' usually requires an indirect object (person) before a 'that' clause.

contrasts.wrong: Could you explain me the new policy changes?
contrasts.right: Could you explain the new policy changes to me?
contrasts.note: 'Explain' takes a direct object (thing) then 'to' + indirect object (person).

contrasts.wrong: My manager suggested me to consider the alternative proposal.
contrasts.right: My manager suggested that I consider the alternative proposal.
contrasts.note: 'Suggest' uses a 'that' clause with a subjunctive or a gerund, not 'to' + infinitive.

contrasts.wrong: The client said me that the project timeline was too ambitious.
contrasts.right: The client said to me that the project timeline was too ambitious.
contrasts.note: 'Say' can take 'to' + indirect object, but not a direct object pronoun.

contrasts.wrong: Please explain me how this new software integrates with our existing systems.
contrasts.right: Please explain to me how this new software integrates with our existing systems.
contrasts.note: 'Explain' requires 'to' before the indirect object when followed by 'how' or 'what'.

drills: The CEO said that market conditions were improving steadily.
She told her team that the deadline was firm.
Could you explain the complex financial model to the new intern?
I suggested that we postpone the decision until next quarter.
He said to his colleague that the report needed revisions.
The consultant explained the strategy to the board members.
They told us that the merger would proceed as planned.
I suggested reviewing the budget before making commitments.
She said that her flight was delayed due to bad weather.
Please explain the process for submitting expense reports.

probes.sentence: The professor explained us the theory in great detail.
answers: The professor explained the theory to us in great detail.
The professor explained to us the theory in great detail.

probes.sentence: My colleague suggested me to take a break from the intense work.
answers: My colleague suggested that I take a break from the intense work.
My colleague advised me to take a break from the intense work.

probes.sentence: He said me that he would handle the negotiations personally.
answers: He said that he would handle the negotiations personally.
He told me that he would handle the negotiations personally.

probes.sentence: The manager told that the project was behind schedule.
answers: The manager told us that the project was behind schedule.
The manager said that the project was behind schedule.

probes.sentence: Can you explain me the implications of this new regulation?
answers: Can you explain the implications of this new regulation to me?
Can you explain to me the implications of this new regulation?

probes.sentence: She suggested me to look into alternative investment opportunities.
answers: She suggested looking into alternative investment opportunities.
She advised me to look into alternative investment opportunities.
